messages:
marta: quick postmortem / follow-up from the FP8 rollout that started friday. we saw a small but consistent quality dip on customer X for long-context prompts :frowning:
alex: saw that in the telemetry — deg_score up ~0.028 on that slice, mostly late tokens. traced to per-layer scale mismatch on certain attention heads.
linh: yup, reproduction points to layer 10/11 for the 7b-family replica. FP8 scale calibration sometimes underestimates headwise dynamic range when past-kv is large.
ben: main ops concern is cost/latency if we add per-layer dithering/corrections. per-layer state multiplies memory and hurts caching.
sam: proposal: add a negotiable "precision-metadata" header that carries a traceable id and small per-request hints (not full per-layer tensors). use it to opt-in customers to conservative profiles.
alex: agreed on metadata. we should also surface a runtime trace id so evals and devtools can correlate tokenwise delta to quant decisions. simple example: header `X-Precision-Trace: p-20260316-az09`
linh: for calibration algorithm, we can do a lightweight per-layer scale correction (single float multiplier) computed from running moments. store that in profile config instead of full tensors. cheap to apply at runtime.
ben: that helps but we still need caching strategy. suggest `profile_cache` with LRU and size cap per model family. evict policy keyed by (model, profile-version, tenant).
sam: rollout plan idea: 1) build profile telemetry (trace id + deg_score) 2) canary shadow route for 3% traffic with new per-layer multipliers 3) automated gating if deg_score > 0.02 for 12h 4) human review 5) promote
alex: also add unit shadow evals: run small reference prompts offline and compare top-k overlap + embedding cosine. the metric should be stable and cheap.
marta: action items: @alex add trace-id header + telemetry keys, @linh prototype per-layer-multiplier store, @ben implement profile_cache LRU, @sam drive canary plan and rollback playbook.
ben: quick config sketch for profile store (suggested format):
```
{
  "profile_version": "v3",
  "model_family": "7b-align",
  "per_layer_multiplier": [1.0, 0.98, 1.02, ...],
  "fallback_policy": "global-scale",
  "evict_ttl_secs": 86400
}
```
linh: note: multipliers should be annotated with calibration confidence. low-confidence ones get slower rollout and double shadowing.
alex: telemetry fields to add: ["precision_trace_id", "profile_version", "deg_score", "late_token_delta", "head_candidates"] — these should be exported to per-tenant dashboards and evals pipeline.
sam: for SLA-sensitive tenants we should allow pinned default profiles and a "safety band" boolean that disables aggressive fp8 lanes automatically. also provide per-tenant opt-out via config API.
marta: timeline: prototype by Wed next week, canary by the following Tue. is that reasonable?
ben: reasonable. I'll start on cache + low-overhead apply path.
linh: I'll hack calibration runner and a small offline analyzer to surface head-wise ranges.
alex: I'll add trace header + wire upthe telemetry schema. small note: include sampling frequency so we don't overload metrics.
sam: I'll write the canary checklist and rollback playbook. include steps: cut traffic to 0, revert profile_version at routing, flush caches, and notify customers.
deploy-bot: canary job queued: build/precision-profiles/canary-1719600000 -> pending
marta: thanks all. small follow-up: let's keep the per-request header size <200 bytes and avoid embedding tensors; the idea is traceability + hinting, not full negotiation. :thumbsup:
alex: one more thought — add an async evaluation endpoint that accepts a trace_id and replays using different profiles to compute delta report. will help triage.
linh: that will be super useful. we can store replay artifacts tied to `precision_trace_id` for 7 days.
ben: ops question: how do we mark a profile as "experimental" vs "trusted"? suggest a metadata field `trust_level: experimental|canary|stable` and routing policy respects that.
sam: good call. include rollout percentage caps for experimental profiles.
marta: ok closing loop here — i'll post a short RFC update with decisions and action items. please update your tickets. :rocket:
